title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Character Select. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Character Select
options.lineage: Arcade and console fighting-game roster screens
options.thesis: Every project is a playable fighter; the recruiter picks one and the footage steps into the ring.
options.viewport: Project select screen: selected project's footage fills a slanted stage with its name in huge condensed italic, a fixed stat block, and the six-project roster grid beside it; a P1 HUD bar carries Francis, Resume, and Contact.
options.risk: Can tip into costume if the slants and splashes outnumber the footage; the video must stay the hero.

raised.raise: One gesture, one transformation: choosing a project runs a single VS-splash transition into its dossier instead of scattered effects.
State is drawn on the surface itself: the selected tile floods with the P1 colour rather than gaining a badge.
Preview before commit: hovering or focusing a roster tile plays that project on the stage before it opens.
Every stat slot owns one fact in a fixed position (engine, platform, role, status) so projects cross-compare at a glance.
One diagonal angle governs every cut, panel, and transition on the page.
A permanent escape route: the HUD's Resume and Contact stay reachable from every screen.

options.label: Console Game Library
options.thesis: The portfolio as a console home screen: each project a game tile that wakes up with its trailer when selected.
options.viewport: A horizontal row of project tiles over the selected game's full-bleed trailer, title and short blurb beneath, and a top bar with profile and resume.
options.risk: Familiar: this is where most game-dev portfolio redesigns land, and it reads like a console clone.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: A flat plane that one pull turns into volume.
options.viewport: A black semicircle that gathers into a project shell.
options.risk: Studio recruiters do not see games in tailoring.
options.case: Loses both axes: no game identity and project content hides behind the cloth.
options.kept: One gesture drives one complete transformation.

options.label: Chromatophore Skin
options.thesis: A living surface that signals state through its own colour.
options.viewport: A pulsing skin where projects surface as patterns.
options.risk: Beautiful, but reads as biology art rather than a developer portfolio.
options.case: Loses both axes: abstract signals obscure which game is which.
options.kept: State lives in the surface, not in badges.

options.label: Algorave Source Floor
options.thesis: Code on the wall changes what happens next.
options.viewport: A stage-scale code buffer driving the reel.
options.risk: Neon-on-black terminal is the category rut for developer portfolios.
options.case: Loses both axes: recruiters skim games, not source buffers.
options.kept: Upcoming changes are previewed before they commit.

options.label: Night Flight Six-Pack
options.thesis: Six calm instruments, each owning one truth.
options.viewport: Projects as six dials on a black panel.
options.risk: Gauges imply numeric metrics the portfolio cannot truthfully show.
options.case: Loses both axes: aviation, not games, and invites invented numbers.
options.kept: Fixed positions, one fact per slot, a cross-check reading order.

options.label: Pulp Rocket Plate
options.viewport: A rocket crossing the frame with the name in speed-lined caps.
options.risk: Retro sci-fi nostalgia, not game development.
options.case: Loses both axes: the world competes with the footage.
options.kept: One diagonal rules the whole composition.

options.label: Night-Market Sign River
options.thesis: Lantern signs lead visitors stall to stall.
options.viewport: A lantern-lit street where each stall is a project.
options.risk: Wayfinding through a street slows recruiters down.
options.case: Loses both axes: charming but indirect for a one-minute skim.
options.kept: A simple escape route stays visible everywhere.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer portfolio: hero, project grid, about, contact, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role headline, a short intro, and a grid of project cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other portfolios, and not game-like at all.
